text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The law assocation deplored the continued boycott of elections by the opposition and urged the government and opposition parties to resolve their differences.
- The Drug Enforcement Commission said it arrested 125 suspects for drug offences last month.
- A South African firm, Afridev, said it was interested in setting up a waste recycling plant in Zambia.
- Police said eight people were killed and six seriously hurt in road crashes in the southern town of Mazabuka on Saturday.
- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy has expelled four officials for allegedly helping a cabinet minister campaign for the presidency in party elections scheduled for 2001.
- The opposition Liberal Progressive Front urged the government to make public the amount earned from sales of state-run enterprises.
- Finance Minister Ronald Penza said there would be no political interference in the operations of the Zambia Revenue Authority.
